crossRefs.note: While the day was coming on, Paul begged them all to take some food, saying, “Today is the fourteenth day that you wait…
Hungry and thirsty, their soul fainted in them.
Then they cried to Yahweh in their trouble, and he delivered them out of their distresses,
When much time had passed and the voyage was now dangerous, because the Fast had now already gone by, Paul admonished…
and said to them, “Sirs, I perceive that the voyage will be with injury and much loss, not only of the cargo and the…
Reuben answered them, saying, “Didn’t I tell you, saying, ‘Don’t sin against the child,’ and you wouldn’t listen?…
When the south wind blew softly, supposing that they had obtained their purpose, they weighed anchor and sailed along…

people.name: Caphtor
people.line: Island home of the Philistines; visited by Paul

people.name: Paul
people.line: Apostle to the Gentiles, author of many NT epistles

translations.web: When they had been long without food, Paul stood up in the middle of them, and said, “Sirs, you should have listened to me, and not have set sail from Crete and have gotten this injury and loss.
translations.bsb: After the men had gone a long time without food, Paul stood up among them and said, “Men, you should have followed my advice not to sail from Crete. Then you would have averted this disaster and loss.
translations.kjv: But after long abstinence Paul stood forth in the midst of them, and said, Sirs, ye should have hearkened unto me, and not have loosed from Crete, and to have gained this harm and loss.
translations.asv: And when they had been long without food, then Paul stood forth in the midst of them, and said, Sirs, ye should have hearkened unto me, and not have set sail from Crete, and have gotten this injury and loss.
